title: Element 9: Work Equipment
learningObjectives: Identify the hazards associated with powered and hand tools
Explain the requirements for machinery guarding
Describe the principles of Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) for energy isolation
Outline the key requirements for mobile plant and vehicles

content.text: Work equipment includes any machinery, tool, appliance, or installation used at work. Hazards from equipment fall into two categories: mechanical and non-mechanical.

rows: Objects or fluids thrown from machinery
Body or clothing drawn into machine
Contact with hot components or emissions

content.text: Guards physically prevent access to dangerous parts of machinery. The hierarchy of guarding:

items: Fixed guard — Permanently attached; provides best protection; removal requires tools. Preferred option.
Interlocked guard — Linked to machine control; machine stops when guard is opened
Adjustable guard — Allows adjustment for different material sizes; worker can still reach danger zone
Self-adjusting guard — Adjusts to workpiece as it passes through; common on woodworking machinery
Distance guard — Prevents reaching the danger zone without entering; photoelectric barriers, safety fences

content.text: A guard must be: strongly constructed, difficult to bypass or defeat, not introduce additional hazards itself, located at safe distance from danger zone, and not unduly restrict the view of the work process.

A safety procedure that ensures hazardous energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, thermal, gravitational, chemical) are isolated and cannot be re-energised while work is being performed on equipment. Also called Isolation or Energy Control.

items: 1. Notify — Tell affected employees that work is about to start
2. Identify energy sources — All sources: electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, stored energy
3. Isolate — Switch off, close valves, block gravity energy
4. Apply lockout devices — Physical locks prevent re-energisation
5. Release stored energy — Bleed lines, discharge capacitors, block moving parts
6. Verify — Test to confirm equipment is de-energised before starting work
7. Perform work — Only authorised personnel in the isolation zone
8. Restore — Remove locks in reverse order; verify area is clear; re-energise

content.text: Only the person who applied a lock can remove it. If multiple people work on equipment simultaneously, each applies their own personal lock (multi-lock hasp). This prevents one worker removing the lock while another is still in the danger zone.

In Gulf O&G, LOTO is always used alongside the Permit to Work system. The 'Isolation Certificate' is a formal document specifying all energy sources that must be isolated before the PTW is issued. Aramco's GI-0002.100 (Electrical Safety) and GI-7.025 (Work Permits) both address isolation requirements in detail.
Work equipment must be regularly inspected and maintained to remain safe. There are three levels of inspection:

items: Pre-use check — By the operator before each use; check for obvious defects, damage, missing guards
Periodic inspection — At defined intervals; by a competent person; formal record
Thorough examination — For safety-critical equipment (lifting equipment, pressure vessels); by competent person as defined in legislation; certification issued

content.text: Vehicle-related incidents (including pedestrian-vehicle collisions) are among the leading causes of fatalities on construction and industrial sites.

items: Segregate pedestrians and vehicles — Separate routes; barriers; clearly marked pedestrian crossings
Visibility — Mirrors, cameras, banksmen for reversing; high-visibility clothing for pedestrians
Speed limits — Enforce 10–15 km/h on sites; speed bumps; signage
Competence — Operators must hold appropriate licences and site-specific authorisation
Pre-use checks — Tyres, brakes, lights, horn, seatbelt, all-round visibility
Safe loading — Never exceed rated capacity; secure loads; no passengers unless seats provided

content.text: A worker is struck by a reversing forklift at a warehouse in Dubai. Investigation reveals: no segregated pedestrian route; forklift had no reversing alarm; driver had no authorisation; area had poor lighting. Corrective actions: install pedestrian barriers and markings; fit reversing cameras and alarms to all forklifts; implement competency-based authorisation; upgrade lighting.
